title: Re-Spread Calculation of the Installment When an Invoice Joins a Plan
content:
Calculation note — **Patient Payment Plans**: the regular installment of an accepted plan on the day an invoice is enrolled on it (the added-invoice installment).

## Formal statement

The added-invoice installment is worked out by re-spreading: the plan's carried balance and the balance due on the invoice being added are spread over the installments still to fall due under the term, but over no more than 9 installments, and the quotient is rounded to the nearest cent, an exact half cent being rounded up.

The carried balance is the invoice balances already enrolled on the plan, less the down payment fixed when the plan was accepted, less every scheduled-installment, arrears, extra-principal and payoff payment on the plan ledger, less every release on the plan ledger; a down payment taken on the invoice being added does not lower the amount spread.

The installments still to fall due under the term are the term's installments less those whose due date has already passed, the passed ones counted as the whole months from the plan's first due date to today plus one.

The new installment applies from the next installment onward, and the added-invoice installment is never more than 25 percent above the installment standing on the plan; when the amount worked out is higher, the added-invoice installment is the standing installment raised by 25 percent, rounded to the nearest cent with an exact half cent rounded up, and the plan runs on until its balance is cleared.

## Quantities

| Quantity | Meaning |
|---|---|
| Invoice balances already enrolled | Every enrollment line on the plan ledger before the new invoice is booked, added together |
| Down payment fixed at acceptance | The down-payment figure on the plan record |
| Payments subtracted | Ledger payments posted as scheduled installments, arrears payments, extra-principal payments or payoffs |
| Releases | Every release line on the plan ledger |
| Balance due on the invoice being added | The balance due the open invoice shows in Patient Invoices & Statements |
| Installment standing on the plan | The regular monthly installment on the plan record at the time of the enrollment |
| Divisor | The installments still to fall due under the term, or 9 if that is fewer |

## Worked note (hypothetical 12-month plan)

Enrollment lines 1,600.00; down payment fixed at acceptance 160.00; four scheduled installments of 120.00 paid (480.00); no other payments or releases; standing installment 120.00. First due date 10 February; today 25 June.

1. Carried balance: 1,600.00 less 160.00 less 480.00 is 960.00.
2. Installments passed: 4 whole months from 10 February to 25 June, plus one, is 5; still to fall due: 12 less 5 is 7, which is not more than 9.
3. The invoice being added has a balance due of 77.00. Spread: 960.00 and 77.00 together, 1,037.00, divided by 7 is 148.142…, that is **148.14**.
4. Ceiling: 120.00 raised by 25 percent is 150.00; 148.14 does not exceed it. The added-invoice installment is **148.14**, from the next installment onward.

**Same plan, larger invoice.** With a balance due of 350.00 the spread is 1,310.00 divided by 7, that is 187.14. This exceeds 150.00, so the added-invoice installment is **150.00** and the plan runs on until its balance is cleared.

**Divisor held at 9.** On an 18-month plan with 3 installments passed, 15 are still to fall due; the spread runs over 9.
